summary: Adds an IMAP extension for creating live, automatically updated search results, something like virtual mailboxes. IMAP search is powerful, but the results are static and awkward to keep current. This standards-track extension lets a client define a context and be told as messages enter or leave it, so results stay current without re-running the search.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5267 lets an IMAP client ask for search or sort results in smaller pieces and receive notices when the matching set changes. A client can use these features to keep a filtered mailbox view current.

questions: what is the imap context extension
what does imap search return update do
subtitle: Adds live update notifications and partial result windows for IMAP search and sort.

tldr.problem: IMAP search results do not update by themselves, and large result lists can be costly to retrieve and keep current.
tldr.mechanism: ESORT adds return options to SORT, while CONTEXT extensions add update notifications and partial result windows to SEARCH and SORT.
tldr.outcome: Clients can maintain changing views of mailbox results without repeating every search. RFC 5267 was updated by RFC 5465 and RFC 9394.

today: RFC 5267 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2008. It has been updated by RFC 5465 and RFC 9394, and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why IMAP Adds Contexts
sections.content:
IMAP search can find matching messages, but the results are static. Large mailboxes can produce more results than a client wants to store, and sorted results are difficult to keep current over a low-bandwidth connection.

RFC 5267 adds ESORT and CONTEXT extensions. They let clients request selected result data, request a window of results, and receive notifications as messages enter or leave a search result.
sections.plainLanguage: An IMAP search returns a result at one point in time. These extensions let a client request only part of a large result and learn when the matching set changes.

sections.title: Extended SORT Results
sections.content:
A server advertising ESORT accepts return options after RETURN in SORT and UID SORT commands. Results arrive in an ESEARCH response and remain in the requested sort order.

The options include MIN, MAX, ALL and COUNT. An empty list requests all results. Ranges in responses are interpreted in increasing numeric order after expansion.
sections.plainLanguage: With ESORT, a client can ask for the count, an endpoint or all sorted matches. The server returns the requested information in the sort order.

sections.title: Contexts and the Reuse Hint
sections.content:
A server advertises CONTEXT=SEARCH or CONTEXT=SORT when it supports the corresponding extension. The added return options are CONTEXT, UPDATE and PARTIAL.

CONTEXT tells the server that the client may repeat the same search criteria. The server MAY ignore the hint or use it to maintain a cache or index. Contexts do not create a snapshot: later searches still reflect the mailbox's current state.
sections.plainLanguage: The CONTEXT option hints that the client may repeat a search. It does not freeze the results; later searches still reflect current messages and flags.

sections.title: Notifications with UPDATE
sections.content:
When a search or sort uses UPDATE, the server sends unsolicited ESEARCH responses with ADDTO and REMOVEFROM entries when matching messages change. Changes can follow new messages, flag changes or expunges. The client processes these entries in order and must not reuse the command's tag while its updates are active.

Updates stop when the mailbox is no longer selected or the client sends CANCELUPDATE. A server can refuse a request with NOUPDATE, but MUST provide at least one updating context per client. It can still honor other return options when it refuses updates.
sections.plainLanguage: UPDATE makes the server report additions and removals as the search results change. The client applies each notice in order and can stop notifications with CANCELUPDATE.

sections.title: Partial Results and Server Caching
sections.content:
PARTIAL asks for a range of positions in the result list. Position 1 is the first result; for example, PARTIAL 1:500 requests the first 500 results. A command cannot contain more than one PARTIAL or ALL option.

Clients may request windows in any order. PARTIAL and UPDATE do not interact, so updates can describe matching messages outside the current window. Servers may cache searches, but MUST return the same results whether or not a cache is used, and must keep any cache current as the mailbox changes.
sections.plainLanguage: PARTIAL lets a client fetch a selected range instead of the whole result list. UPDATE can still report changes outside that range because the two options work independently.

sections.title: Security and Context Limits
sections.content:
The RFC says these IMAP capabilities do not change the underlying security considerations and are not believed to introduce new security issues. It warns that authorized users could create many contexts and consume server resources.

Servers can limit the number of active contexts, refuse excess update requests using the defined response, and log context creation and use. SORT contexts may require more server resources than SEARCH contexts.
sections.plainLanguage: Keeping many searches updated can consume server resources. A server may limit active contexts and refuse additional update requests when needed.
